notes: TWO templates, one persona. (1) `Kinetic Business by Windstream`, the gold layout: a three-column header/value pair, `Account number Telephone number Invoice date` on one line and the three values on the next, so one anchor yields three fields. (2) `Windstream Enterprise`, carried in `anchor_alts` on every selector: same three-column idea but the labels are stacked over TWO lines (`Account Invoice Total` / `Number Date Amount Due` / values), so nothing spells `Account Number` or `Total Amount Due` as a contiguous run and each alt anchors a header row read across instead. Its summary ladder is reworded throughout (`Previous Total`, `Payments Applied`, `New Charges - Due by <date>`, `TOTAL INVOICE AMOUNT`) and it prints no telephone number and no separate `Due date` label. The two vocabularies are disjoint, so an alt is unreachable on a Kinetic bill and a primary is unreachable on an Enterprise one; `tests/packs/test_windstream_enterprise_template.py` asserts that, because it is what makes one persona safe for both. The sole exception is the brand name, which is on both - which is why `remit_address` is the one selector ordered the other way round, Enterprise label first and the bare `WINDSTREAM` anchor demoted to the alt: as the primary it matched the word inside a sentence of portal boilerplate and returned a paragraph. `vendor_name` is read ONLY on the Enterprise template, and that asymmetry is the point. The Kinetic text layer breaks the brand mid-word (`Kinetic Business by Windstre am`), so no pattern can capture it and the pack's display-name table has to supply it; the Enterprise brand IS readable (`ATTN: Windstream Enterprise Services`, present natively and surviving OCR), so the selector reads it and `resolve_vendor_alias` leaves the printed value alone rather than overwriting it with the table's single Kinetic-oriented entry. Printed evidence wins where it exists; the table is for where the print is unreadable. Both still collapse to the one `windstream` canonical (F5).
